#1574. Cucurella defends Vinicius Jr over Diomande comparison as Real Madrid pause eight-game winning run

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 20:52

Marc Cucurella has defended Vinicius Junior amid the Brazilian’s difficult start to the season, insisting that team-mate Yan Diomande does not help him more defensively than the Real Madrid forward does. Real Madrid have paused an eight-game winning run for the international break, during the best spell under boss Jose Mourinho, and are hoping Vinicius rediscovers his form with Brazil under Carlo Ancelotti. Cucurella shares that wish.

Speaking on the Cope radio programme El Partidazo, the Spanish left-back was asked about the poor start to the season of Vinicius, who has just one goal and three assists in 12 matches. The decline in his form, together with a suspension that kept him out of the last four La Liga games, has led to the meteoric rise of Diomande, who has made a difference on the left side.

Beyond four goals and four assists in 16 matches, the Ivory Coast forward has been praised for his tactical commitment, helping Cucurella with defensive recovery. But the Real Madrid number 17 rejects the idea that Diomande helps him more with marking than the Brazilian does.

‘I do not think he helps me more, I think he is more visible,’ Cucurella said. ‘Diomande runs back and is everywhere. Vinicius goes back three times and then, the fourth time he does not run, the ball is played in. If Vini scored three goals per game, nobody would say anything to him.’

Days after his signing from Chelsea was announced in late June, the defender told Radio Marca that he ‘did not mind’ if Vinicius ‘does not track back or help in defence’, because he wanted the number seven energised to have an impact in the final third with goals. Cucurella also told Vinicius that he would do all the ‘dirty work’ for him.

Despite that consent, the forward has helped with the compactness without the ball, following the Portuguese boss’s guidance. The main problem is that, in possession, the 26-year-old has not shown the same efficiency as in recent years in dribbles in one-on-one situations and in decision-making.

Like other figures at Real Madrid, the Spaniard came out in defence of Vinicius, considering a dip in form natural after consecutive seasons among the best players in the world. The left-back also insisted that Vinicius has been working behind the scenes to react and regain his prominence, which he considers fundamental to Mourinho’s success in 2026-27.

‘Vinicius is a player who has been performing at a spectacular level for five years, so it is understandable that he is going through a difficult phase now,’ Cucurella continued. ‘I see that he is motivated and works hard in training, and that is what matters.’

‘The most important thing for us is that he returns to his best level, because if he is at his peak, we have a great team,’ he concluded.

#1572. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

FT |⌛️| Finisce in parità all’Allianz Stadium#JuveSRFC #UEL pic.twitter.com/QaF2LuUDp9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 22, 2026

Krogh had refereed nine Europa League matches and one Champions League match before this game. He had never taken charge of either club.

Juventus’s next Europa League fixtures are away to AZ Alkmaar on 5 November 2026 and at home to Omonia on 26 November 2026. Before that, Serie A resumes. Lecce host Juventus on matchday 8, with Eusebio Di Francesco’s side kicking off against Spalletti’s at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday 25 October.

#1571. Barcelona Women vs Arsenal Women - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 21:06, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 21:08

Arsenal Women will travel to the Camp Nou for Thursday's highly anticipated meeting with reigning European Champions Barcelona Women.

The Gunners are sitting in fifth spot in the Women's Champions League league phase, while the Catalan giants are flying high at the top of the standings with a perfect record.

Barcelona have made the perfect start to their bid to win a fifth UWCL title, having won their opening three league phase games by a combined 19-2 scoreline.

After comfortably dispatching Paris FC and Roma, Barcelona made light work of their clash against Koge on matchday three, with Claudia Pina netting a brace in an emphatic 8-0 victory in Denmark.

Barcelona returned to Liga F action with a 4-0 success against fellow Catalan side Badalona, before they eased to a 5-1 victory in Sunday's meeting with Madrid CFF, moving them four points clear of second-placed Real Madrid at the top of the standings.

Those two league wins have helped Barcelona build a four-game winning run since suffering a surprise 2-1 away loss against Real Sociedad on October 18.

While they experienced a blip on their travels, Barcelona have won all six of their competitive home games this season, scoring at least five goals in five of those victories.

The Blaugrana have also won 33 of their 35 UWCL home games (D1, L1), including each of their last 11 European home assignments since losing 1-0 to Chelsea in the first leg of their semi-final tie in April 2024.

Arsenal, meanwhile, have struggled for consistency in domestic action this season, with Renee Slegers's side sitting in sixth spot and six points adrift of the top three after recording three wins, four draws and two defeats in nine Women's Super League games.

Having taken seven points from their three European games, the Gunners are at least in a better position in the Women's Champions League, even if their first two performances were far from convincing.

Arsenal required a 93rd-minute penalty to see off Koge on matchday one, before they spurned a goal lead in a frustrating 2-2 draw against Paris FC in the French capital.

The Gunners at least made light work of their home game against Benfica, which saw Alessia Russo net a hat-trick in a commanding 3-0 victory at Meadow Park to become the leading English scorer in UWCL history with 23 goals.

Russo went on to score in a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa before registering a brace in Sunday's 2-1 away win over Liverpool, meaning she has now scored nine goals in Arsenal's last seven competitive matches.

The in-form forward will be hoping to continue her impressive form in Thursday's fixture, as Arsenal look for a repeat of the memorable 1-0 victory they recorded in their most recent meeting with Barcelona in the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon.

Barcelona Women Women's Champions League form:

Arsenal Women Women's Champions League form:

Barcelona boss Pere Romeu remains without the services of Laia Aleixandri, Kika Nazareth and Vicky Lopez due to injury.

Kerolin has also been added to the injury list, having been ruled out for around four weeks with a calf problem.

Renee van Asten, Patri Guijarro and Aitana Bonmati could all come into the side after dropping down to the bench for the win over Madrid CFF.

As for the visitors, they are expected to be without Mariona Caldentey, Selina Cerci, Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang, while there are doubts surrounding the availability of Stina Blackstenius and Chloe Kelly.

Defender Taylor Hinds is also an injury concern after being withdrawn in the closing stages of the win over Liverpool.

Former Barcelona full-back Ona Batlle is expected to return to the squad after sitting out Sunday’s game with a knock.

While Arsenal are yet to lose in Europe this season, there is no tougher European fixture than facing Barcelona at the Camp Nou, and considering the home side's impressive home record, we think the reigning UWCL champions will pick up a comfortable victory.

#1570. Ivory Coast vs Gambia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 10 Nov 2026 21:27, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 21:28

Ivory Coast and The Gambia will be looking to maintain their perfect starts to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they meet at Stade de la Paix in Bouake on Thursday evening.

Both teams have collected six points from their opening two Group C matches, and Thursday's encounter represents the first of two meetings between the sides in five days, with the return fixture scheduled to take place in The Gambia on November 17.

Ivory Coast have made an encouraging start under returning head coach Herve Renard, who began his second spell in charge with two wins from two competitive matches before suffering a friendly defeat to Cameroon.

His return opened with a 2-0 victory over Ghana, with Malick Yalcouye opening the scoring before Franck Kessie converted a second-half penalty, and the Elephants followed that result with another 2-0 win against Somalia, as Bazoumana Toure and Yann Gboho found the net.

The Elephants are yet to concede in the qualifying campaign and will be hoping to maintain that defensive record against The Gambia on Thursday, having won their last four meetings with the Scorpions while scoring nine goals and conceding none.

Ivory Coast also boast an impressive home record in this fixture, having won all three previous meetings on their own soil, scoring eight goals without conceding.

While the Elephants have been particularly solid defensively at the start of this campaign, The Gambia's attacking firepower has been central to their own impressive opening, with the Scorpions scoring six goals across their first two qualifiers.

They began with a 2-1 victory over Somalia before producing an impressive comeback to beat Ghana 4-2 away from home, with Ebrima Colley scoring three goals across the two matches, including a brace against the Black Stars.

The West African side will be looking to make it three consecutive victories, a feat they have not achieved in the last five years, with that run predating Johnny McKinstry's appointment as head coach in June 2024.

However, one concern for the visitors will be their lack of defensive solidity, having failed to keep a clean sheet in their last five matches, although they have managed to score 10 goals during that period.

Ivory Coast Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Gambia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Amad Diallo has returned to the Ivory Coast squad after overcoming an injury concern, providing Renard with another attacking option for the double-header.

However, the Elephants will be without Odilon Kossounou and Guela Doue, who are both sidelined through injury, while Wilfried Singo, Simon Adingra, Evann Guessand and Sebastien Haller have not been included in the squad.

The Gambia have been boosted by the returns of Musa Barrow and Yankuba Minteh, who have both recovered from the injuries that kept them out of the September qualifiers.

Alieu Fadera and Adama Sidibeh are unavailable through injury, while James Gomez has not been included in the final squad.

Jesper Ceesay and Suleiman Camara have also withdrawn because of injuries, with Saidou Khan and Salieu Drammeh called up as their replacements.

The Gambia's attacking form makes it difficult to envisage another straightforward clean sheet for Ivory Coast, but the hosts have shown greater defensive control and possess enough quality in the final third to break down an organised defence, making them favourites to claim all three points.

#1569. CM: Milan begin initial discussions over renewal for Musah – the situation

Yunus Musah has been one of the surprises of the season for AC Milan. Now, the management have begun talks over his contract.

Calciomercato.com begin a report on Musah by recalling what Sky pundit Alessandro Florenzi – a former Milan player himself – said to the midfielder live on air after the Rossoneri’s derby win over Inter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

“I congratulate you because you’ve had two difficult years. I know you’re a guy who’s suffered a lot, but you’ve never given up,” the former full-back said.

“I can assure you of this because I’ve watched you work together for years. It’s truly been a great pleasure, so congratulations, and don’t get too big for your boots, but I’m sure you won’t because you’re a good guy.”

These were sincere words from someone who has experienced the Milan dressing room and knows how difficult it can be to succeed.

One of the key figures behind Musah’s new-found form is Ruben Amorim. The Portuguese coach completely revitalised him after two very difficult seasons, relying on him from day one and receiving a lot of hard work and dedication in return.

Amorim’s vision demands a player with Musah’s characteristics: a powerful engine, a remarkable ability to transform a passive game into an active one, and excellent transition skills. Versatility helps too, given that against Genoa the manager even deployed him as a left-back.

Musah’s season so far has seen him make 11 league appearances, with a total of 759 minutes played, plus three in the Europa League, with 222 minutes played. Going into preseason, that kind of reliance seemed impossible.

It’s not just Amorim who’s satisfied with Musah’s performances but the entire management as well, so much so that in recent days they’ve even discussed the possibility of extending his contract, which expires in 2028.

Recent contacts with the player’s entourage have helped them begin evaluating the possibility of renewing his deal. Musah currently earns around €2m per season and – if he maintains this level – he will sign new terms before the end of the season.

#1568. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

Sources: Juventus FC, Tuttosport, Virgilio Sport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1567. Albania vs Finland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 10 Nov 2026 22:13

Albania could secure promotion from League C of the Nations League by beating visitors Finland at Arena Kombetare on Thursday.

The hosts are first in their four-team group with nine points from a possible 12, whereas Finland are third with seven points and could be eliminated if they lose.

Albania concerningly needed a 93rd-minute penalty to beat San Marino 2-1 on October 6 in their most recent Nations League outing, and a similarly wasteful evening at Arena Kombetare may prove costly.

It should be noted that while the hosts could secure first place with a win, Belarus are second with seven points and would have to lose against San Marino on Thursday for that to occur.

The Red and Blacks have so far scored eight goals in the Nations League while conceding on just three occasions, and they have kept two clean sheets.

Boss Rolando Maran has only overseen six games - three wins and three losses - but he should be delighted by the fact the national team have won three of their last four matches considering they lost their prior five fixtures.

Albania will hope to win a third consecutive clash at home, but a defeat would be their fourth in six contests when playing as hosts.

Finland suffered a 1-0 loss against Belarus in the Nations League on October 6, conceding the winner in the first minute after an incredible strike from range.

That result left them behind Belarus due to their head-to-head record despite the fact they have the best goal difference in the group having netted nine times while only conceding twice.

The visitors managed to win 2-1 against Albania in the reverse fixture on October 3, and they have in fact won four and drawn one of their past five encounters with their hosts.

Head coach Jacob Friis's side have only lost one of their four most recent matches, though they have been beaten in four of their last seven games.

Huuhkajat's record on their travels has been poor considering they have been defeated in seven of their last 10 outings on the road, claiming victory just once.

Albania centre-forward Rey Manaj is a likely inclusion given he has netted twice in the Nations League so far, and he may be flanked by Ernest Muci and Arber Hoxha.

Elsewhere, expect to see Ylber Ramadani and Kristjan Asllani together in a double pivot, while Klisman Cake, Ardian Ismajli and Mario Mitaj could feature in a three-man defence.

Goalkeeper Etrit Berisha was sent off in that Finland clash in October, though he has served his suspension and is available for selection on Thursday.

Finland are almost certain to field a similar lineup to the one that beat Albania in their first meeting in the Nations League, with Leo Walta set to start having scored both goals from midfield in that victory.

Samuli Miettinen and Miro Tenho can be pencilled into the backline, while Joel Pohjanpalo is a likely candidate to start up front.

Berisha; Cake, Ismajli, Mitaj; Hysaj, Ramadani, Asllani, Pilios; Muci, Manaj, Hoxha

Hradecky; Stahl, Miettinen, Tenho, Lahteenmaki; Kairinen, Markhiev, Walta; Svanback, Pohjanpalo, Hakans

Thursday's clash will almost certainly be closely fought, and both teams will likely create opportunities.

However, it is difficult to ignore Finland's inconsistencies on the road, and given Albania have improved considerably at home, the hosts should be seen as favourites at Arena Kombetare.

#1566. Senegal vs Sudan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 10 Nov 2026 23:08

Senegal host Sudan in Group J of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying at Stade Leopold Sedar Senghor in Dakar on Thursday.

The Lions of Teranga are unbeaten but have scored only twice in two games, while the Falcons of Jediane arrive third on three points after a 4-1 defeat in Maputo.

Senegal are second in Group J on four points, level with Mozambique but behind them on goal difference, +1 to +3.

Patrick Vieira's first competitive game in charge ended 1-1 away to Mozambique on September 25, and Senegal then edged Ethiopia 1-0 in Bahir Dar four days later through Ibrahim Mbaye's 11th-minute goal despite 61% possession.

The 1-0 friendly win over Comoros in Marseille on October 4, settled by Iliman Ndiaye's fifth-minute goal, made it three games in a row with a single Senegal goal and only one conceded across them.

Off the pitch, Ismail Jakobs has retired from international football, and Sadio Mane asked to be excused from the squad to stay home with his family.

Vieira's second squad includes four first call-ups, Pathe Mboup, Pape Demba Diop, Clayton Diandy and Paul Mendy, and does not include Idrissa Gana Gueye.

Senegal have not lost in eight meetings with Sudan, winning five and drawing three, the latest a 3-1 victory in the Africa Cup of Nations last 16 in Tangier on January 3 in which Pape Gueye scored twice before half time.

Sudan are third in Group J on three points with two goals scored and four conceded, and both of their goals have come from penalties.

Mohamed Eisa converted an 86th-minute penalty to beat Ethiopia 1-0 in Juba, the capital of South Sudan, on September 25, a result that briefly took the Falcons of Jediane top of the group.

Mozambique then won 4-1 in Maputo on September 29, with Witi scoring in the 24th minute, Chamito adding a brace, Guima making it 3-0 in the 58th minute and Yaser Hamed pulling one back from the spot in the 88th.

Kwesi Appiah, the Ghanaian head coach, took Sudan to the last 16 of the January tournament, where Abdallah, a semi-professional at an Australian second-tier club in Melbourne, gave them a sixth-minute lead before Senegal replied three times.

Several of Appiah's players come from Al Hilal and Al Merrikh, and the return leg against Senegal follows on Monday, November 16.

Senegal Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Sudan Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Mamadou Sarr is out with a left calf injury sustained in Real Sociedad's 1-1 Europa League draw with Lyon, and the club has indicated he will miss at least two to three weeks.

Krepin Diatta was forced off in Watford's Championship match against Middlesbrough on November 7 and has been replaced in the squad by the Sevilla defender Arouna Sangante.

Habib Diarra, Ismaila Sarr and Abdallah Sima are also unavailable, which leaves Nicolas Jackson, Mbaye, Ndiaye and Boulaye Dia as the main attacking options.

With Jakobs retired, El Hadji Malick Diouf is the left-back option, and Kalidou Koulibaly captains a back line that also includes Moussa Niakhate.

For the visitors, no injury or suspension has been reported ahead of the trip to Dakar.

Mohamed Eisa and Yasin Hamed have found the back of the net from the spot against Ethiopia and Mozambique respectively, and will hope to get a goal from open play against Senegal.

Diaw; Sy, Koulibaly, Niakhate, El Hadji Malick Diouf; Pape Gueye, Camara; Mbaye, Pape Matar Sarr, Ndiaye; Jackson

Both of Sudan's goals in this campaign were penalties, so they have yet to create a clear chance from open play, and Senegal have conceded only once in three matches under Vieira.

Senegal's three straight one-goal games are the genuine concern, but Sudan conceded four in Maputo and three in Tangier in January, and Jackson and Mbaye combined for the winner in Bahir Dar.

Absences such as Mane, Diatta and Sarr thin the squad, yet the Koulibaly and Niakhate pairing remains intact and should be enough to keep out a Sudan attack whose only goals so far came from the penalty spot.

#1565. GdS: The full story of Milan and Inter’s record-breaking €650m deal with Generali

More details continue to emerge regarding the stadium naming rights deal between AC Milan, Inter and Generali.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that even before it’s even been built, the new home of Milan and Inter is already the place to be. It’s no coincidence that Generali – the insurance giant – has decided to put its stamp on the façades, as was revealed last month at the presentation of the stadium.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The collaboration kicks off immediately. Generali are now the Official Insurance Partner of the two clubs. The stadium naming rights contract will last for 25 years and includes the payment of €50m until the stadium opens in 2031.

This includes €10m annually for each of the next five seasons, including the current one, to be split equally between Inter and Milan. Once the stadium is inaugurated, the sum will increase to €30m annually (€15m each) for the following 20 years. The total commitment amounts to €650m.

Generali wanted to associate its name with the stadium from the very beginning of this long journey, in order to establish itself in the collective imagination: it will only be the Generali Stadium, with no temporary or secondary names to muddy the waters.

Branding a stadium from day one – or rather, even before it opens – is particularly strategic in terms of marketing. For this reason, Generali have agreed to pay €10m a year for something that, for five years, will be on models and then on construction sites, but not yet in the experience of fans.

Moreover, the naming rights market still has ample room for development in Europe. A Kroll study of the 36 major European clubs highlighted this already in 2024: only 12 had sold the naming rights to their stadiums, for a total estimated potential value of €303m, equivalent to an average of €8.4m per season.

Italy and England were the leagues least inclined to this form of commercialisation, also held back by the historical connection between the stadiums and their names. In this scenario, the new Inter and Milan stadium represents a different opportunity: a stadium to be built around a commercial identity,.

It’s not just a sports sponsorship: it’s a key support for a project crucial to the next stage of development of the city, the beating heart of the country’s economy and finances. This explains the significant investment.

It was the first time Inter and Milan worked together on the same side of the table, to secure a commercial deal. Under the watchful eye of Oaktree and RedBird Capital, the two clubs’ Chief Revenue Officers – Giorgio Ricci and Maikel Oettle – took the lead in finalising the sale of the naming rights.

These will be transferred through Stadio San Siro, a company controlled by NSM Holding, equally owned by Milan and Inter. The Rossoneri and Nerazzurri had initially selected a small group of potential partners, focusing on major Italian companies.

This type of right is particularly attractive to companies with a strong interest in the local area. After an initial round of meetings, Generali was the company that immediately showed the most enthusiasm.

Inter and AC Milan thus decided to further discuss the deal with the insurance giant, finalising the contract within a few months, the largest ever signed by Generali in the sports sector. In addition to the price offered, a key factor was the partner’s status.

Who better than the insurance giant – with €4.3bn in net profit and €900bn in assets under management – can offer guarantees of solidity and solvency, especially in a long-term commitment?

The €650m is written in stone and represents a significant portion of the financial coverage for the entire real estate transaction. Moreover, thanks to the €50m ‘bridge’ payment, the clubs have the opportunity to cash in immediately.

A comparison with other major international stadiums further illustrates the scale of the operation. Once fully operational, with €30m annually, the Generali Stadium will rank at the top of the global naming rights market, becoming one of the most lucrative deals ever signed for a stadium.

In Europe, the benchmark is Spotify’s Camp Nou, which guarantees Barcelona €20m per season, while Bayern Munich earn around €13m annually from Allianz for the Munich Arena. London’s Emirates Stadium is currently worth an estimated €10-15m to Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano is at a similar level to that of the Gunners. In Germany, Borussia Dortmund get around €11m for Signal Iduna Park. Juventus, with the Allianz Stadium, earns around €8-10m.

To find higher figures, one must look primarily to the United States, where the stadium sponsorship market is of a different size and characteristics. The Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles is worth approximately €31m annually, but the $700m twenty-year contract also includes other commercial activities of the AEG group and partnerships with the Lakers and Kings.

The same is true for SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, whose twenty-year, $625m agreement equates to approximately €28m annually, but includes additional commercial components. Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, on the other hand, has signed a thirty-year agreement worth approximately $750m, equivalent to approximately €22m per season.

These transactions should be interpreted with caution, as the consideration does not always refer solely to the naming of the stadium. The Milan figure, however, is significant precisely because of the size of the naming rights component.

There is also another aspect to consider. The €30m guaranteed by Generali could represent only the first step in a much broader commercial strategy. An ecosystem of partnerships will develop around the new stadium, from technology services to beverage supplies, and other product categories that can be accommodated in the facility.

The goal is to raise an additional €20-25 million through agreements with secondary sponsors, bringing the overall value of the stadium’s commercial partnerships to even higher levels. Meanwhile, the market is also starting to move in Italy, albeit on a much smaller scale.

Atalanta earn approximately €2.5m annually from its partnership with New Balance for the naming of the New Balance Arena, while Udinese earns approximately €1m Bluenergy for the Bluenergy Stadium.

In short, the Milan deal risks rewriting the industry benchmarks, pushing up the valuations of other European venues and confirming how the name of a stadium, when associated with an international project, is a valuable asset.could become a top-level commercial asset.

#1564. 'People keep telling me it's great I'm managing against my son... it's not - it's horrible': Peterborough boss ROBBIE SAVAGE and Reading star CHARLIE on their 'awkward' FA Cup showdown, playing for Man United and dangers facing modern young players

Published: 02:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EST, 7 November 2026

The FA Cup cast its spell upon the Savages while they were out shopping for groceries.

Reading midfielder Charlie was strolling the aisles of the Marks & Spencer foodhall with his girlfriend when his phone began to buzz. He remembered it was first-round draw day.

He fished out the phone, saw the cascade of messages and realised, as they like to say in M&S, this was not just any FA Cup draw. He called his dad.

Peterborough United boss Robbie was in the Co-op. He had stopped on his way back to the rented lodgings he describes as a 'little annexe in someone's garden' and was rummaging through the ready meals in search of a spaghetti bolognese for one when he answered.

'The reception in Peterborough isn't great, it kept cutting out,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Charlie said: "You won't believe the draw." I thought he was going to say Forest Green. Or Macclesfield. I didn't think about Reading. He said: "You've got us." I just went: "Oh no."'

They were on a collision course from the moment Robbie left Forest Green for the Posh job last month. The teams were scheduled to meet in League One next month at Reading but the FA Cup draw caught them off guard.

Peterborough boss Robbie Savage (right) with his son, Reading midfielder Charlie. The pair will meet in the FA Cup first round at London Road on Saturday

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport

And while they were both at great pains to stress that Saturday's tie at London Road, screened live on TNT Sports, is about Peterborough and Reading not their little family gathering, they can appreciate the fuss.

'Football is a beautiful game, it brings people together and creates rivalries,' says Charlie. 'This week it's created a rivalry in our family. I'm not sure who my mum, brother, grandparents and cousins will support but there's no better time for them to have a half-and-half scarf.'

For Robbie, the beauty of the occasion is yet to unfurl itself. 'It's going to be horrible,' he says. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling. People keep telling me it's great. I've got to say it's not great, it's horrible. Usually we speak every day and I've not been able to speak to him all week because I don't want to put him in a position where anything gets out and anyone can point a finger at him.

'I don't want it to be billed as Savage v Savage because it's not. Charlie might not play but if he plays and makes a mistake and we score the winner, so be it. If he plays and scores the winner, well, wow.'

Robbie puffs out his cheeks and widens his eyes as he considers this scenario. 'We've got to win for Peterborough United,' he adds.

Ironically, it was a passion relit by coaching his sons which tempted the former Leicester, Birmingham and Blackburn midfielder out of the comfort of his media work and into coaching. Savage helped out with his youngest son Freddie's Under 13s team in the Timperley and District Junior Sunday League.

'Standing out at training on a Tuesday and Thursday night,' says Robbie. 'Sunday morning, putting the nets up. I've been that dad. In the first season we were hammered 13-0, but we built a team and won a lot of things.'

Charlie Savage in action for Reading. The midfielder played 45 games for the club last season but has yet to start a league match during this campaign

Savage offers some advice to his team in his new role as manager of Peterborough

Two years ago, Charlie and Freddie implored their father to follow his heart and make the switch from sporting director to manager at Macclesfield in the Northern Premier League.

'Even back then, he said one day he'd manage against me,' Charlie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I was in League One and he was in Step Three and I'm thinking, "Well, give it a few years", but he always gets where he wants to get to.

'He's a competitor. He wants to win, wants to succeed. Even with my little brother's team it hurt him to lose in Sunday morning grassroots football. That's something inside him and it won't change.

'He will want to beat us. Unfortunately for him, I'm the same. I want to win. There might be an awkward car journey home.'

Charlie's memories of his father playing football are from Derby, the last stop of a 15-year professional career which started at Manchester United and took in seven different clubs, as well as 39 Wales caps. 'I remember seeing his long hair, scurrying around the pitch,' says the 23-year-old. 'Throwing his arms up and shouting at the refs.'

Like his dad, Charlie also came through United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

'He'll always have that on me,' says Robbie. 'All I ever wanted to do from 14 to 19 was play for one minute in Manchester United's first team. It didn't happen and he's done it. His name is on the wall at Carrington and mine isn't.

'I'm so glad his name is there instead of mine. You want the best for your sons. I'm proud of both my sons.'

Charlie has three Wales caps and counting. His father won 39...

...but despite both Charlie and Robbie coming through the Manchester United academy, only Charlie played for the first team (above), against Young Boys at Old Trafford in 2021

Freddie is studying for an economics degree at the University of Manchester. Charlie left United for Reading four years ago and now has 175 senior appearances and three Wales caps under his belt and a reputation in his own right.

'He's got a great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie. 'He's intelligent. Nine As in his GCSEs. He doesn't drink, he lives his life 24 hours a day, seven days a week to be a footballer. He's a down-to-earth, humble kid.

'He was so brave to go and play senior football when he had three years left at Manchester United, and it's paid off. He played 45 games last season. He hasn't started a league game this season but hasn't sulked.

'I was a sulker, as Martin O'Neill and Nigel Clough (who coached Savage at Leicester and Derby respectively) will tell you. If that was me, my body language would be negative, but he's got a great attitude. And I've tried to tell him now he has to train harder than ever and conduct himself in the right way.'

If Robbie is a guiding light and inspiration for Charlie, vital information flows both ways for an aspiring manager with a young team.

'The mindset of a Millennial is completely different to when I played,' says the 52-year-old Posh boss. 'If they're not in the team or the manager has shouted at them, they go home to an apartment where they live alone away from their families, isolated from 2pm to 7am with all that time to think about it.

'We have to understand their vulnerabilities on and off the pitch. Charlie has been through that so without knowing it, he's made me a better manager. I try to think about what's best for my players, what I'd want a manager to do for Charlie in that situation.'

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end,' Charlie says of his dad Robbie

'Great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie of his son Charlie

Being the Son of Sav cannot be easy. Not only the added scrutiny and expectation, and accusations doors have been opened for him by a famous and influential father, but also in a world where footballers are too often considered fair game for abuse whether inside the stadium or online.

'It's there in all forms of life,' admits Charlie. 'Maybe people subconsciously want me to fail a little bit more because of who he is. I get it. Football is a game and my dad is a divisive figure inside that game.

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end. Sometimes the abuse goes too far. People forget he's a human not just a football personality.

'But I wouldn't change who he is. I wouldn't change having him as my dad, I'm very proud of him.'

#1563. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

At Juve FC, Luca covers match analysis, squad news, and the longer threads that run through a Juventus season. He writes with the perspective of someone who genuinely cares about where the club is heading rather than simply reporting what has already happened. His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

By Alexis Pereira | 10 Nov 2026 23:14

BlueCo and the City Football Group are reportedly following the progress of Fredrikstad winger Gabriel Wesseh, with offers expected for the 18-year-old American in the next transfer window. The right winger left the United States last summer to join the Norwegian club from Atlanta, and he is already attracting attention in the Eliteserien.

Wesseh was born in the United States and came through the Philadelphia academy, so this is his first experience abroad. The United States Under-19 international has settled well in the Norwegian top flight. Since his arrival, he has made 15 appearances, six of them as a starter, scoring four goals and providing two assists.

#1561. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa new boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery said. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

“Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia shows his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

“We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we showed a really good character.”

And that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Though Savio takes the corner quickly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

The Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his new club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

So close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

Huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

But the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus

And as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2

Back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer

Predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

Boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

Joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

McGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

Another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

Villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

But Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

Spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

Marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

Villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

Jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

Four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

It’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

Porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

Early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

He had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the issue here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

Savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

Watch for some long balls from Tyrone Mings down the channels for Nicolas Jackson today. The pair had a little chat before kick-off with Jackson seemingly telling Mings where he wants the ball launched to.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.

Both teams are coming out of the tunnel now, greeted with plenty of noise from the home and away fans.

The stakes are very high for a match so early on the season and kick-off here we come!

This is the second fixture of the week, as Brentford stormed past Chelsea last night 3-0.

Nottingham Forest vs Coventry (Sat 5.30pm)

Led out by the skipper 🫡 pic.twitter.com/5MLh8ZpvU4

It's almost time ⏰#COYS pic.twitter.com/EewgmTnngl

Just heard on TNT that Newcastle have won more games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in 2026 than Tottenham have...

An early goal here for Villa could be catastrophic for the home team.

Neither club have had any players called up for England, but plenty of players will be leaving to join up with their national teams abroad.

From Spurs, Pedro Porro has retained his place in Spain’s squad. Both Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke have been called up for the Netherlands and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky will join the Czech Republic squad, still awaiting his first senior cap.

Among the Villa players to receive call-ups, Johan Manzambi will be leaving to join the Switzerland squad, while captain John McGinn has been called up for Scotland once again. Zion Suzuki will leave to join Japan in the three-week break as well.

No Mathys Tel in the Spurs squad. De Zerbi has given him plenty of chances, but Tel has always been one of the first players the head coach has criticised this season.

"I don't see any player that would strike fear into me."Steven Gerrard and Glenn Hoddle give their thoughts on Spurs' transfer business and current squad 💰🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eM22XDDAjs

Who is the superstar that Spurs need? Join the conversation and let us know who you think is the missing piece in the comments section.

“We have to improve in everything, because like I said, after the game we conceded the first goal in a bad way, because we knew what was the plan in the defensive phase. One long ball on Gakpo is not enough to concede a goal. Also the second goal could have closed Gakpo better and stronger, and the third goal is an individual skill of Szoboszlai.

“We can improve in the qualities of the play. I think we created more chances than the other games, also because Liverpool played with more courage.

“There was more space to attack, to make one-to-one, but I have experience enough to say that sometimes when you are the coach of the team, without you knowing the reason, you are able to score, you can score. And other times, another situation where I think you are playing well, not fantastic, but well enough to score, enough to win, and you don’t win.

“You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence. We move on and we keep going to be better day by day, but not by words, but by fact.”

“Similar, like us, but their potential is a huge potential. They signed, spending, a lot of very good players, but they need as well, time to get compact everything and to achieve understanding their idea.

“Of course, (Roberto) De Zerbi, he’s a fantastic manager. He played fantastic football here and performed fantastic here in Brighton. He did a fantastic job before as well, in Shakhtar, and in Italy, and after Brighton, a fantastic job in Marseille.

“And now, when I can watch them, they are in this process, but of course, they are getting better, they compete fantastic, even losing against Liverpool.

“Of course, being very, very demanding defensively for us, trying to impose and dominate our moment with the ball as well during the game. This is the challenge. Of course, Tottenham, I expect them to be in the top four.”

Two changes for Villa from the side that lost to Nottingham Forest, with Johan Manzambi and Joao Gomes entering the mix. It’s a first full debut for Manzambi since joining the club from Freiburg over the summer. Gomes returns having served his suspension following a red card against Brighton on the opening weekend.

Representing Aston Villa ✊ pic.twitter.com/5xnjiPnRny

Only one change from the team that faced Everton, as Pedro Porro returns to the starting XI, replacing Archie Gray. Carabao Cup goal-scorer Connor Gallagher is on the bench.

Our Spurs side to face Villa 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Xgpl4Hx9VV

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

#1560. CorSport: Krösche, Hardung and three signings – Milan preparing for frantic January

AC Milan have shown both their potential and their limitations this season, leading to a desire to do business once the window reopens.

According to Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) this morning, the head coach Ruben Amorim has made it clear both publicly and privately that he needs deeper and more competitive squad in order to achieve consistency in results and performance levels.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

When the coach has had to rotate, the team suffers. Gerry Cardinale has promised significant reinforcements, and the first piece of the new structure will be Markus Krösche, set to become Head of Football on January 1st. But the German executive may not arrive alone.

Timmo Hardung – Krösche’s long time right-hand man at Eintracht Frankfurt and RB Leipzig – could follow him to Italy. The two have worked side by side in recent years, and Milan are considering re-creating the tried-and-tested management duo.

Should Hardung decide to leave Eintracht, the chances of him joining Milan are very real, as even Sky Germany have admitted. Meanwhile, Krösche is already working on the plans fr the future, although he’ll need to wait a few months before taking office.

In the winter window, the Rossoneri intend to acquire three players. A central defender remains the absolute priority, while a left-back is also being sought, in addition to a striker capable of acting as an alternative to Gonçalo Ramos.

The goal is therefore to increase the squad’s depth, especially given the difficulties encountered in midweek matches and with making multiple changes. No names are mentioned specifically, but the target has been set ahead of a potentially busy January.
